LESSON: KENYAN FOLK SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.1: Kenyan Folk Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Folk Songs, part of Performing in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does exposure to various performances influence an individual’s response to folksongs? 2. Why are Kenyan folk songs important in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Folk Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner listens critically to Kenyan folk songs and identifies their

characteristics.

● Citizenship: The learner appreciates listening to and performing folksongs from different social cultural groups

in Kenya.

● Digital Literacy: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology to record own

performances to share with others.

Values:
● Patriotism: The learner appreciates performing folk songs from different Kenyan communities.

● Unity: The learner collaborates with peers to perform Kenyan folk songs.

● Responsibility: The learner makes appropriate use of digital devices with appropriate assistive technology

when recording and uploading music performances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Safety and security: The learner takes precaution while interacting with digital devices with appropriate

assistive technology as they record and share the performances with peers for feedback.

● Self-esteem: The learner gains confidence as they perform Kenyan folk songs before an audience.

Suggested Learning Resources

Traditional musical instruments, Resource persons, Costumes and props, Audio/visual recordings of folk songs,

Exercise books in appropriate print, ICT devices, Braille equipment and materials,

Suggested Key Skills Assessed

• Describing characteristics of Kenyan folk songs.

• Selecting a Kenyan folksong for performance.

• Performing a Kenyan folksong applying performance aspects.
